public_rationale: The historical concern about combining structured representations remained recognizable in controlled contemporary generalization failures. Broader evaluations also found substantial recurring errors across model families. These records support the modest claim that several old concerns persisted. They do not support an assertion that the field had made no progress: scale and prompting improved performance.
limitations: BIG-bench deliberately includes difficult tasks; its aggregate results are not an everyday error rate.
The historical paper's stronger architectural conclusions are not established by these modern evaluations.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns recurring problems in combining familiar parts, transferring rules to unfamiliar cases, and producing correct answers. It does not assert that every historical criticism remains valid.
For the ongoing state, use the latest completed research year, 2022, plus the portion of 2023 preceding the post. Research evaluations have no standard quarterly reporting period.
The older criticism supplies historical context; contemporary evaluations must establish persistence.
Improved performance is compatible with unresolved problems.
criteria.support_condition: Independent contemporary evaluations show recurring failures across several of the named concerns, and the historical record establishes that these concerns predate the current revival.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Broad contemporary evaluations establish reliable performance on the named abilities, leaving only isolated examples that do not sustain the claim of recurring problems.

evidence.explanation: The original paper establishes the historical concern about compositional and systematic representations. Its March publication is recorded conservatively at month end; it does not establish the performance of modern models.

evidence.publisher: arXiv; Najoung Kim, Tal Linzen and Paul Smolensky
evidence.explanation: Controlled changes to COGS exposed failures to transfer familiar linguistic components into new contexts in T5. This directly supports persistence of compositional generalization problems, rather than merely unfamiliar-word recognition problems.

The evaluation finds persistent errors across a broad collection of reasoning and knowledge tasks and multiple model families. The same section reports improvement with model scale and examples, so these results support remaining weaknesses rather than no progress.

The study shows that prompting can improve the composition of intermediate answers. This limits a stronger interpretation that the old problems had seen no meaningful progress, but does not establish their general solution.
